Muqatil said: the dwellings of 'Ad were in Yemen, in Hadramawt, at a place called Mahra, to which camels are attributed, so it is said: "Mahri camels" and "mahari" (she-camels). They were people of tents that moved about in spring, and when the pasture was lush, they returned to their dwellings. They were from the tribe of Iram.

Al-Dahhak said: al-Ahqaf is a mountain in Syria. Mujahid said: it is the land of Jasaq from Hismā. Qatada said: it has been mentioned to us that 'Ad were a people in Yemen, people of sand dunes overlooking the sea, in a land called al-Shihr. Ibn Zayd said: al-Ahqaf is what stretches of sand are like a mountain, without reaching the status of a mountain. [[See al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/43, at the verse.]]

Al-Kalbi said: al-Ahqaf is what the water receded from at the time of the flood, the water receding from the earth and leaving its trace. Al-Khalil said: they are great sand dunes. Al-Kisa'i said: they are sand that is curved, and its singular is ḥaqf and ḥiqāf, like dabagh and dibagh, and libs and libas. It was also said: ḥaqāf is the plural of ḥaqf, and aḥqāf is the plural of the plural.

The analogue of ḥaqf/aḥqāf is shabr/ashbār. Al-A'sha said:

"So he spent the night beside a tamarisk-covered dune, wrapped by a burning north wind that leaves the face ashen."

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/29.]]

And he said: "Between us a parched valley with winding dunes." It is said: ḥaqf, aḥqaf, meaning sand fully curved. Al-'Ajjaj said:

"He spent the night beside a tamarisk-covered dune, a dune bent."

Its verb is aḥqafa. The rajaz poet said:

"The crescent moon's edge until it bent."

That is, it inclined and curved.

﴿And warnings had already passed﴾, the messengers had passed on. ﴿from before him﴾, that is, before Hud, ﴿and from after him﴾, which in the reading of 'Abd Allah is "and after him." ﴿that you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great day.﴾ They said: ﴿"Have you come to us to turn us away﴾, to divert us ﴿from our gods? Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful."﴾ He said: ﴿"The knowledge is only with Allah﴾, of the time when the punishment will come, ﴿not with me, and I convey to you that with which I have been sent, but I see you as an ignorant people."﴾

﴿Then when they saw it﴾, meaning the punishment, ﴿as a cloud﴾, placed in the accusative as a circumstantial state; or if you wish, by repetition, meaning "they saw it as a cloud." It is the cloud, named so because it appears across the sky, meaning it shows itself on the breadth of the heavens.

Mujahid said: it swept them into the valley. Al-A'sha said:

"O you who see a cloud, I have spent the night watching it, as if lightning in its edges were torches."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/33.]]

The exegetes said: Allah drove the black cloud which Qayl ibn 'Anz had chosen, having returned with what it contained of vengeance to 'Ad, and it came out upon them from a valley of theirs called al-Mughith. They had been deprived of rain for days, so when they saw it...

[They said: "This is a cloud bringing us rain," until a woman among them named Mahdar recognized that it was a wind, and she cried out and fainted. When she recovered, it was said to her: "What did you see?" She said: "A wind in which were meteors of fire."] [[Tafsir al-Tha'alabi: 3/46 at the verse; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/235; Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/285.]]

﴿heading toward their valleys﴾, they rejoiced at it.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 46, verse 13–25 (part 2 of 2):

They said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Nay, it is that which you were seeking to hasten: a wind wherein is a painful punishment.﴾ So it began to carry off the tent and the litter-bearing camel, lifting them up until they appeared like locusts.

Ibn Manjuwayh informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah related to us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Kisa'i related to us: al-Harith ibn 'Abd Allah related to us: Hushaym related to us, from Juwaybir, who related to us: Abu Dawud al-A'ma, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿But when they saw it as a cloud coming toward their valleys﴾, to the end of the verse, he said:

When the cloud drew near, they stood up and stretched out their hands. The first thing by which they recognized that it was a punishment was that they saw what was outside their dwellings, their baggage and their livestock, being carried by the wind between the sky and the earth like the pigeons (rushā). They said: So they entered their houses and closed their doors. But the wind came, forced their doors open and threw them down. Allah commanded the wind, and it poured sand over them, so they were beneath the sand for seven nights and eight days, ﴿in succession, desolate﴾, groaning. Then Allah commanded the wind, and it removed the sand from them; then He commanded it, and it carried them away and cast them into the sea.

They are the ones of whom Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Destroying everything by the command of its Lord﴾ — it passed over the men of 'Ad and their wealth — ﴿by the permission of its Lord﴾.

Ibn Manjuwayh informed us: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl related to us: Abu Hisham related to us: Hafs related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to be alarmed when he saw the wind, and he would say: "O Allah, I ask You for its good, the good within it, and the good it has been sent with; and I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil within it, and the evil it has been sent with." [8] [[Sahih Muslim: 3/26; al-Sunan al-Kubra 3/360.]]

When he saw a sign of rain (mukhīlah), he would stand up, sit down, come and go, and his color would change. So we would say, "O Messenger of Allah, [why?]" He would say:
"I fear that it may be like the people of 'Ad, of whom they said: ﴿This is a cloud bringing us rain.﴾" [9] [[Ibid.]]

﴿So they became such that nothing was seen except their dwellings.﴾ Al-Hasan recited (لا تُرى) with a dammah on the tā' and إِلَّا مَساكِنُهُمْ with a raf' on the nūn. Similarly, Shu'ayb ibn Ayyub related it from Yahya ibn Adam, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, from 'Asim.

Abu Hatim said: This is not sound in the language unless one posits an implied elision (idmar), as you say in speech: "The women do not see except Zaynab," but you cannot say "does not see except Zaynab." Sibawayh said: its meaning is "(does not see) their persons" — إِلَّا مَساكِنُهُمْ. Al-Farra' considered this verse to be an irregular construction (istikrah), and he mentioned that al-Mufaddal recited to him:
"Our fire has not seen a fire like it; Ma'add knows this well, in generosity"
He made the verb feminine (fa-annatha fi'l mithl) because it refers to the fire. He said: The most eloquent speech would be to say: "Lam tara mithlaha nar" (no fire has seen the like of it). [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/36.]

Al-A'mash, 'Asim, Hamzah, Ya'qub and Khalaf recited (بياء) with a dammah on the yā', مَساكِنُهُمْ in the nominative, and Abu 'Ubaydah and Abu Hatim preferred the nominative. Al-Kisa'i said: its meaning is "nothing is seen except their dwellings."

Al-Farra' said: people are not seen because they were under the sand, so only their dwellings are seen, since they are standing.

The rest recited (تَرى) with a fatḥah on the tā' and (مساكنَهم) in the accusative, on the meaning: "you (O Muhammad) do not see except their dwellings."

﴿Thus do We recompense the guilty people.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 46, verses 13–25 (part 1 of 2)**

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve. Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein, as a reward for what they used to do.﴾ ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents.﴾ The common readers recite "ḥusnan" without an alif. The people of Kufa recite "iḥsanan," and this is the reading of Ibn 'Abbas. [[It is said that in the codices of the people of the two sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), Basra and Syria, the reading is "ḥusnan." Their proof is the words of the Exalted in Surat al-'Ankabut (29:8): ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Raja' recite "ḥasanan," with a fatḥa on the ḥa and the sīn. The proof of the common readers is the words of the Exalted in Surat al-An'am (6:151): ﴿and to parents, kindness﴾, and this is in the codices of the people of Kufa. (See Zad al-Masir: 6/121, and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/192.) I say: in the codices of the Muslims in this age the reading is "iḥsanan," and our proof is the words of the Exalted: ﴿and do not separate﴾.]]

﴿His mother bore him with hardship﴾, with difficulty and hardship. ﴿and she gave birth to him with hardship﴾, and ﴿his bearing and his weaning﴾, that is, his weaning from milk, ﴿is thirty months﴾. Al-Hasan and Ya'qub recite "wa-faṣluhu" without an alif. The exegetes said: his gestation was six months and his suckling was twenty-four months.

Ibn Ishaq said: his gestation was nine months and his weaning from milk was twenty-one months.

﴿Until, when he reaches his full strength﴾, the height of his power and stature and the peak of his youth and maturity, which is between eighteen and forty years of age. This is the meaning of His words, ﴿and reaches forty years﴾. Al-Suddi and al-Dahhak said: this verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. The story has already passed. Others said: it was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) and his father, Abu Quhafa 'Uthman ibn 'Amr, and his mother, Umm al-Khayr bint Sakhr ibn 'Amr ibn 'Amir. When Abu Bakr reached forty years, he believed in the Prophet (ﷺ) and said to his Lord: ﴿Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed I am among the Muslims.﴾

Ibn Manjawayh informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us: Ishaq ibn Sadaqa related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim related to us, from Sayf ibn 'Umar, from 'Atiyya, from Abu Ayyub, from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning His words: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾. It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr. Both of his parents embraced Islam, and no one among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah from among the Emigrants had both parents embrace Islam except him. Allah enjoined him concerning them, and this continued after him.

He said: ﴿My Lord, enable me﴾, inspire me and grant me capacity, ﴿to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness which You approve, and make righteous for me my offspring﴾, that You make them believing and righteous. They said: Allah answered Abu Bakr concerning his children, and they embraced Islam. No Companion other than Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) had himself, his parents, his sons and his daughters all embrace Islam.

﴿Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed I am among the Muslims.﴾ ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did﴾, meaning their righteous deeds, so He rewards them for them.

﴿And We overlook their misdeeds﴾, so He does not punish them for them. ﴿among the companions of Paradise﴾, that is, along with the companions of Paradise. The "fī" here means "with." ﴿the true promise which they were promised﴾, and it is His words: ﴿Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. [[Surat al-Tawba: 72.]]

﴿And he who says to his parents, when they call him to faith in Allah and affirmation of the Resurrection and the Recompense: "Uff to you both!"﴾ That is a word of aversion.

﴿"Do you promise me that I will be brought forth﴾ from my grave alive after my death and my decay?" The common readers recite "a-taʿidāninī" with two genuine nūns, while the people of Syria recite it with one doubled nūn. ﴿while generations have passed before me﴾, and none of them was resurrected. Al-Hasan, al-A'mash and Abu Ma'mar recite "an akhraja" with a fatḥa on the "rā'" and a ḍamma, [i.e., "an ukhraja" in the passive is read differently].

﴿And the two of them call upon Allah for help﴾, seeking His aid against him and saying to him: ﴿Woe to you! Believe, for indeed the promise of Allah is true.﴾ ﴿But he says, "This is not but the fables of the former peoples."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliya, al-Suddi and Mujahid said: this verse was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah. It was also said: it was revealed concerning 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq. His parents said to him: "Embrace Islam," and they insisted on calling him to faith. He said: "Bring back to life for me 'Abd Allah ibn Jud'an, 'Amir ibn Ka'b and the elders of Quraysh, so that I may ask them about what they say."

Muhammad ibn Ziyad said: Mu'awiya wrote to Marwan that the people should pledge allegiance to Yazid. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr said: "You have brought it as a Heraclian [monarchy], will you pledge allegiance to your sons?"

Marwan said: "This is the one about whom Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the one who says to his parents, 'Uff to you both! Do you promise me...﴾" to the end of the verse. 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her) heard of this and became angry, and she said: "By Allah, it is not about him. If I wished, I could name him, but Allah cursed your father while you were in his loins, so you are a son of the curse of Allah."

﴿Those are the ones against whom the word has come into effect﴾, meaning the punishment became obligatory for them. They said: that refers to those whom Ibn Abi Bakr indicated, and he said "bring them to me," and they are the ones against whom the word has come. They are the ones who passed away, as in His words: ﴿while generations have passed before me﴾. As for Ibn Abi Bakr, Allah answered his father's supplication in His words: ﴿and make righteous for me my offspring﴾, so he embraced Islam and his Islam was good.

Al-Hasan and Qatada said: this verse is general in its reference, and it describes a disbelieving, wicked servant who is disobedient to his parents. ﴿among nations﴾, along with nations ﴿which passed away before them, of jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers.﴾ ﴿And for each [of the two groups], the believers and the disbelievers, there are degrees﴾, ranks and levels with Allah on the Day of Resurrection according to their deeds, and He will recompense them for them. Ibn Zayd said: in this verse, the degrees of the people of the Fire go downward, and the degrees of the people of Paradise go upward.

﴿And that He may fully pay them their deeds﴾, their rewards, with the "yā'" (third person) read by Makki, Basri and Hisham, and the rest read it with the "nūn" (first person plural). ﴿and they will not be wronged.﴾

﴿And on the Day the disbelievers are exposed to the Fire﴾, it will be said to them: ﴿"You used up your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them﴾." Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir and Ya'qub recite "adhhabtum ṭayyibātikum" in the interrogative form, and it is differently reported from the people of Syria and others in the declarative form. Both are sound and eloquent, because the Arabs use the interrogative for reproach and omit the interrogative particle in it. So they say: "Did you go, and do such-and-such?" and "You went and did, and did?"

﴿So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you were arrogant about on earth without right, and for what you used to defy.﴾

Ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Manjawayh informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah related to us: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Karabisi related to us: Humayd ibn al-Rabi' related to us: Abu Ma'mar related to us: 'Abd al-Warith related to us: Muhammad ibn Hujara related to us, from Humayd al-Shami, from Sulayman, from Thawban, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Whenever the Messenger of Allah traveled, the last person he left was from his family, and the first person he entered upon when he returned was Fatima (peace be upon her)."

When he returned from a campaign and came to her, he glimpsed [something] at her door, and he saw on al-Hasan and al-Husayn two silver bracelets. So he turned back and did not enter upon her. When Fatima saw that, she thought he had not entered upon her because of what he had seen. So she tore the curtain and removed the two bracelets from the boys and cut them. The boys wept, so she divided it between them in two halves. They went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while weeping, and the Messenger took it from them and said: "O Thawban, take this to the house of so-and-so, the people of a household in Medina, and buy for Fatima a necklace of ʿaṣab and two bracelets of ivory." He said: "Indeed these are the people of my household, and I do not wish that they should use up their good things in the life of this world." [5] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/275; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/43.]]

'Aqil ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed us: Muhammad ibn Jarir informed us: Kathir related to us: Yazid related to us: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, who said: a companion of ours related to us, from Abu Hurayra, who said: "Our food with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was only the two blacks: water and dates. By Allah, we did not see these your sumra (a kind of tree) and we did not know what they were."

And with the same chain, from Qatada, from Abu Burda ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qays al-Ash'ari, from his father, who said: "O my son, if you had witnessed us while we were with our Prophet (ﷺ), when the rain befell us, you would have thought our smell was the smell of sheep. Our clothing was only wool."

And with the same chain, from Qatada, who said: it has been mentioned to us that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say: "If I wished, I could be the best of you in food and the softest of you in clothing, but I hold back my good things." It was also mentioned to us that when he came to Syria, a meal was prepared for him the like of which he had never seen. He said: "This is for us. So what about the poor Muslims who died while they never had enough of barley bread?" Khalid ibn al-Walid said: "They have Paradise." 'Umar's eyes welled up with tears, and he said: "If our share is in the goods and they have departed, while in my view they are in Paradise, then indeed they have left us far behind."

It has also been mentioned to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon the People of the Suffa, a place where the poor Muslims gathered, and they were patching their garments with leather, finding no patches for them. He said: "Are you today better, or on a day when one of you goes out in one garment and comes back in another, and a bowl is brought to him in the morning and another in the evening, and he curtains his house as the Ka'ba is curtained?" They said: "We are better on that day."

Al-Husayn ibn Manjawayh informed us: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Nasrawayh related to us: Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Musa al-Jawhari related to us: 'Ali ibn Sahl al-Ramli related to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us: Razq Abu al-Hudhayl related to me: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah related to me, from Ibn 'Abbas, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), that he related to him that he entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he had abandoned his wives. He found him on a rough, rumpled bed, meaning a mat, a rope bed, the mat having left its mark on his side, reclining on a leather pillow stuffed with palm fiber.

'Umar said: "I looked around the room, and by Allah I did not see anything that would catch the eye except a hide, meaning a damaged skin, whose smell had spread. So I wept, and I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you are the Messenger of Allah and His chosen one, while, as I see it, Kisra and Caesar are in brocade and silk!'" Then the Messenger of Allah sat up and said: "Are you in doubt, O son of al-Khattab? Those are a people whose good things were hastened to them in their worldly life." [6] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/34.]]

Ibn Manjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Utba related to us: al-Furmani related to us: Abu Umayya al-Wasiti related to us: Yazid ibn Harun related to us: Mubarak ibn Fudala informed us: Hafs ibn Abi al-'As related to us, who said: "I used to have lunch with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and our lunch was bread with oil and vinegar, bread with milk, bread with dried meat, and the least of it was broad meat." He used to say: "Do not sift the flour, for all of it is food." [7]

Then he would bring thick, coarse bread, and he began to eat and said to us: "Eat!" So we began to make excuses, and he said: "What is the matter with you that you do not eat?" I said: "By Allah, O Commander of the Faithful, we do not eat it. We return to a food softer than your food."

He said: "Bah, O son of Abi al-'As! Do you not see that I know how to command that the flour be sifted with a cloth and baked in such and such a way? Do you not see that I know how to command that a fat kid goat be brought, its hair removed, and it come out roasted like such and such? Do you not see that I know how to command that a sa' or two sa's of raisins be made, placed in a waterskin, and water poured over them, and it is cooked until it becomes like the blood of a gazelle?"

He said: I said: "By Allah, O Commander of the Faithful, I see you as one who knows the pleasures of living well." 'Umar said: "Indeed, by Allah, besides whom there is no god, were it not that I fear my good deeds may be diminished on the Day of Resurrection, I would have shared with you in the living. But I heard Allah say concerning a people: ﴿You used up your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them﴾." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/624, no. 35924.]]

Ibn Manjawayh informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us: Muhammad ibn Bakkar al-Rayyan related to us: Abu Ma'shar related to us, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said:

My family craved meat, so I passed by 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), and he said: "What is this, O Jabir?" I said: "My family craved meat, so I bought meat for a dirham." He said: "Whenever one of you craves something, does he put it into his belly? Do you not fear that you may be among the people of this verse: ﴿You used up your good things in your worldly life﴾?"

Ibn Manjawayh informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us: Bishr related to us: Ibn Abi al-Khusayb related to us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Musa informed me: Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari related to us: my father related to us, who said: Wahb ibn al-Ward said: "The son of Adam was created with bread accompanying him, and whatever is added to bread increases appetite." He said: I related this to Abu Sulayman, and he said: "He is right. Salt with bread is a craving."

﴿And mention the brother of 'Ad﴾, meaning Hud (peace be upon him).

﴿when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: al-Ahqaf is a valley between 'Uman and Mahra. Muqatil said: the dwellings of 'Ad were in Yemen, in Hadramawt, at a place called Mahra, to which camels are attributed, so it is said: "Mahri camels" and "mahari" (she-camels). They were people of tents that moved about in spring, and when the pasture was lush, they returned to their dwellings. They were from the tribe of Iram.

Al-Dahhak said: al-Ahqaf is a mountain in Syria. Mujahid said: it is the land of Jasaq from Hismā. Qatada said: it has been mentioned to us that 'Ad were a people in Yemen, people of sand dunes overlooking the sea, in a land called al-Shihr. Ibn Zayd said: al-Ahqaf is what stretches of sand are like a mountain, without reaching the status of a mountain. [[See al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/43, at the verse.]]

Al-Kalbi said: al-Ahqaf is what the water receded from at the time of the flood, the water receding from the earth and leaving its trace. Al-Khalil said: they are great sand dunes. Al-Kisa'i said: they are sand that is curved, and its singular is ḥaqf and ḥiqāf, like dabagh and dibagh, and libs and libas. It was also said: ḥaqāf is the plural of ḥaqf, and aḥqāf is the plural of the plural.

The analogue of ḥaqf/aḥqāf is shabr/ashbār. Al-A'sha said:

"So he spent the night beside a tamarisk-covered dune, wrapped by a burning north wind that leaves the face ashen."

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/29.]]

And he said: "Between us a parched valley with winding dunes." It is said: ḥaqf, aḥqaf, meaning sand fully curved. Al-'Ajjaj said:

"He spent the night beside a tamarisk-covered dune, a dune bent."

Its verb is aḥqafa. The rajaz poet said:

"The crescent moon's edge until it bent."

That is, it inclined and curved.

﴿And warnings had already passed﴾, the messengers had passed on. ﴿from before him﴾, that is, before Hud, ﴿and from after him﴾, which in the reading of 'Abd Allah is "and after him." ﴿that you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great day.﴾ They said: ﴿"Have you come to us to turn us away﴾, to divert us ﴿from our gods? Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful."﴾ He said: ﴿"The knowledge is only with Allah﴾, of the time when the punishment will come, ﴿not with me, and I convey to you that with which I have been sent, but I see you as an ignorant people."﴾

﴿Then when they saw it﴾, meaning the punishment, ﴿as a cloud﴾, placed in the accusative as a circumstantial state; or if you wish, by repetition, meaning "they saw it as a cloud." It is the cloud, named so because it appears across the sky, meaning it shows itself on the breadth of the heavens.

Mujahid said: it swept them into the valley. Al-A'sha said:

"O you who see a cloud, I have spent the night watching it, as if lightning in its edges were torches."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/33.]]

The exegetes said: Allah drove the black cloud which Qayl ibn 'Anz had chosen, having returned with what it contained of vengeance to 'Ad, and it came out upon them from a valley of theirs called al-Mughith. They had been deprived of rain for days, so when they saw it...

[They said: "This is a cloud bringing us rain," until a woman among them named Mahdar recognized that it was a wind, and she cried out and fainted. When she recovered, it was said to her: "What did you see?" She said: "A wind in which were meteors of fire."] [[Tafsir al-Tha'alabi: 3/46 at the verse; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/235; Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/285.]]

﴿heading toward their valleys﴾, they rejoiced at it.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 46, verse 13–25 (part 2 of 2):

They said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Nay, it is that which you were seeking to hasten: a wind wherein is a painful punishment.﴾ So it began to carry off the tent and the litter-bearing camel, lifting them up until they appeared like locusts.

Ibn Manjuwayh informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah related to us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Kisa'i related to us: al-Harith ibn 'Abd Allah related to us: Hushaym related to us, from Juwaybir, who related to us: Abu Dawud al-A'ma, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿But when they saw it as a cloud coming toward their valleys﴾, to the end of the verse, he said:

When the cloud drew near, they stood up and stretched out their hands. The first thing by which they recognized that it was a punishment was that they saw what was outside their dwellings, their baggage and their livestock, being carried by the wind between the sky and the earth like the pigeons (rushā). They said: So they entered their houses and closed their doors. But the wind came, forced their doors open and threw them down. Allah commanded the wind, and it poured sand over them, so they were beneath the sand for seven nights and eight days, ﴿in succession, desolate﴾, groaning. Then Allah commanded the wind, and it removed the sand from them; then He commanded it, and it carried them away and cast them into the sea.

They are the ones of whom Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Destroying everything by the command of its Lord﴾ — it passed over the men of 'Ad and their wealth — ﴿by the permission of its Lord﴾.

Ibn Manjuwayh informed us: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl related to us: Abu Hisham related to us: Hafs related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to be alarmed when he saw the wind, and he would say: "O Allah, I ask You for its good, the good within it, and the good it has been sent with; and I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil within it, and the evil it has been sent with." [8] [[Sahih Muslim: 3/26; al-Sunan al-Kubra 3/360.]]

When he saw a sign of rain (mukhīlah), he would stand up, sit down, come and go, and his color would change. So we would say, "O Messenger of Allah, [why?]" He would say:
"I fear that it may be like the people of 'Ad, of whom they said: ﴿This is a cloud bringing us rain.﴾" [9] [[Ibid.]]

﴿So they became such that nothing was seen except their dwellings.﴾ Al-Hasan recited (لا تُرى) with a dammah on the tā' and إِلَّا مَساكِنُهُمْ with a raf' on the nūn. Similarly, Shu'ayb ibn Ayyub related it from Yahya ibn Adam, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, from 'Asim.

Abu Hatim said: This is not sound in the language unless one posits an implied elision (idmar), as you say in speech: "The women do not see except Zaynab," but you cannot say "does not see except Zaynab." Sibawayh said: its meaning is "(does not see) their persons" — إِلَّا مَساكِنُهُمْ. Al-Farra' considered this verse to be an irregular construction (istikrah), and he mentioned that al-Mufaddal recited to him:
"Our fire has not seen a fire like it; Ma'add knows this well, in generosity"
He made the verb feminine (fa-annatha fi'l mithl) because it refers to the fire. He said: The most eloquent speech would be to say: "Lam tara mithlaha nar" (no fire has seen the like of it). [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/36.]

Al-A'mash, 'Asim, Hamzah, Ya'qub and Khalaf recited (بياء) with a dammah on the yā', مَساكِنُهُمْ in the nominative, and Abu 'Ubaydah and Abu Hatim preferred the nominative. Al-Kisa'i said: its meaning is "nothing is seen except their dwellings."

Al-Farra' said: people are not seen because they were under the sand, so only their dwellings are seen, since they are standing.

The rest recited (تَرى) with a fatḥah on the tā' and (مساكنَهم) in the accusative, on the meaning: "you (O Muhammad) do not see except their dwellings."

﴿Thus do We recompense the guilty people.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 46, verses 13–25 (part 1 of 2)**

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve. Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein, as a reward for what they used to do.﴾ ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents.﴾ The common readers recite "ḥusnan" without an alif. The people of Kufa recite "iḥsanan," and this is the reading of Ibn 'Abbas. [[It is said that in the codices of the people of the two sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), Basra and Syria, the reading is "ḥusnan." Their proof is the words of the Exalted in Surat al-'Ankabut (29:8): ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Raja' recite "ḥasanan," with a fatḥa on the ḥa and the sīn. The proof of the common readers is the words of the Exalted in Surat al-An'am (6:151): ﴿and to parents, kindness﴾, and this is in the codices of the people of Kufa. (See Zad al-Masir: 6/121, and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/192.) I say: in the codices of the Muslims in this age the reading is "iḥsanan," and our proof is the words of the Exalted: ﴿and do not separate﴾.]]

﴿His mother bore him with hardship﴾, with difficulty and hardship. ﴿and she gave birth to him with hardship﴾, and ﴿his bearing and his weaning﴾, that is, his weaning from milk, ﴿is thirty months﴾. Al-Hasan and Ya'qub recite "wa-faṣluhu" without an alif. The exegetes said: his gestation was six months and his suckling was twenty-four months.

Ibn Ishaq said: his gestation was nine months and his weaning from milk was twenty-one months.

﴿Until, when he reaches his full strength﴾, the height of his power and stature and the peak of his youth and maturity, which is between eighteen and forty years of age. This is the meaning of His words, ﴿and reaches forty years﴾. Al-Suddi and al-Dahhak said: this verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. The story has already passed. Others said: it was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) and his father, Abu Quhafa 'Uthman ibn 'Amr, and his mother, Umm al-Khayr bint Sakhr ibn 'Amr ibn 'Amir. When Abu Bakr reached forty years, he believed in the Prophet (ﷺ) and said to his Lord: ﴿Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed I am among the Muslims.﴾

Ibn Manjawayh informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us: Ishaq ibn Sadaqa related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim related to us, from Sayf ibn 'Umar, from 'Atiyya, from Abu Ayyub, from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning His words: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾. It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr. Both of his parents embraced Islam, and no one among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah from among the Emigrants had both parents embrace Islam except him. Allah enjoined him concerning them, and this continued after him.

He said: ﴿My Lord, enable me﴾, inspire me and grant me capacity, ﴿to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness which You approve, and make righteous for me my offspring﴾, that You make them believing and righteous. They said: Allah answered Abu Bakr concerning his children, and they embraced Islam. No Companion other than Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) had himself, his parents, his sons and his daughters all embrace Islam.

﴿Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed I am among the Muslims.﴾ ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did﴾, meaning their righteous deeds, so He rewards them for them.

﴿And We overlook their misdeeds﴾, so He does not punish them for them. ﴿among the companions of Paradise﴾, that is, along with the companions of Paradise. The "fī" here means "with." ﴿the true promise which they were promised﴾, and it is His words: ﴿Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. [[Surat al-Tawba: 72.]]

﴿And he who says to his parents, when they call him to faith in Allah and affirmation of the Resurrection and the Recompense: "Uff to you both!"﴾ That is a word of aversion.

﴿"Do you promise me that I will be brought forth﴾ from my grave alive after my death and my decay?" The common readers recite "a-taʿidāninī" with two genuine nūns, while the people of Syria recite it with one doubled nūn. ﴿while generations have passed before me﴾, and none of them was resurrected. Al-Hasan, al-A'mash and Abu Ma'mar recite "an akhraja" with a fatḥa on the "rā'" and a ḍamma, [i.e., "an ukhraja" in the passive is read differently].

﴿And the two of them call upon Allah for help﴾, seeking His aid against him and saying to him: ﴿Woe to you! Believe, for indeed the promise of Allah is true.﴾ ﴿But he says, "This is not but the fables of the former peoples."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliya, al-Suddi and Mujahid said: this verse was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah. It was also said: it was revealed concerning 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq. His parents said to him: "Embrace Islam," and they insisted on calling him to faith. He said: "Bring back to life for me 'Abd Allah ibn Jud'an, 'Amir ibn Ka'b and the elders of Quraysh, so that I may ask them about what they say."

Muhammad ibn Ziyad said: Mu'awiya wrote to Marwan that the people should pledge allegiance to Yazid. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr said: "You have brought it as a Heraclian [monarchy], will you pledge allegiance to your sons?"

Marwan said: "This is the one about whom Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the one who says to his parents, 'Uff to you both! Do you promise me...﴾" to the end of the verse. 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her) heard of this and became angry, and she said: "By Allah, it is not about him. If I wished, I could name him, but Allah cursed your father while you were in his loins, so you are a son of the curse of Allah."

﴿Those are the ones against whom the word has come into effect﴾, meaning the punishment became obligatory for them. They said: that refers to those whom Ibn Abi Bakr indicated, and he said "bring them to me," and they are the ones against whom the word has come. They are the ones who passed away, as in His words: ﴿while generations have passed before me﴾. As for Ibn Abi Bakr, Allah answered his father's supplication in His words: ﴿and make righteous for me my offspring﴾, so he embraced Islam and his Islam was good.

Al-Hasan and Qatada said: this verse is general in its reference, and it describes a disbelieving, wicked servant who is disobedient to his parents. ﴿among nations﴾, along with nations ﴿which passed away before them, of jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers.﴾ ﴿And for each [of the two groups], the believers and the disbelievers, there are degrees﴾, ranks and levels with Allah on the Day of Resurrection according to their deeds, and He will recompense them for them. Ibn Zayd said: in this verse, the degrees of the people of the Fire go downward, and the degrees of the people of Paradise go upward.

﴿And that He may fully pay them their deeds﴾, their rewards, with the "yā'" (third person) read by Makki, Basri and Hisham, and the rest read it with the "nūn" (first person plural). ﴿and they will not be wronged.﴾

﴿And on the Day the disbelievers are exposed to the Fire﴾, it will be said to them: ﴿"You used up your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them﴾." Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir and Ya'qub recite "adhhabtum ṭayyibātikum" in the interrogative form, and it is differently reported from the people of Syria and others in the declarative form. Both are sound and eloquent, because the Arabs use the interrogative for reproach and omit the interrogative particle in it. So they say: "Did you go, and do such-and-such?" and "You went and did, and did?"

﴿So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you were arrogant about on earth without right, and for what you used to defy.﴾

Ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Manjawayh informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah related to us: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Karabisi related to us: Humayd ibn al-Rabi' related to us: Abu Ma'mar related to us: 'Abd al-Warith related to us: Muhammad ibn Hujara related to us, from Humayd al-Shami, from Sulayman, from Thawban, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Whenever the Messenger of Allah traveled, the last person he left was from his family, and the first person he entered upon when he returned was Fatima (peace be upon her)."

When he returned from a campaign and came to her, he glimpsed [something] at her door, and he saw on al-Hasan and al-Husayn two silver bracelets. So he turned back and did not enter upon her. When Fatima saw that, she thought he had not entered upon her because of what he had seen. So she tore the curtain and removed the two bracelets from the boys and cut them. The boys wept, so she divided it between them in two halves. They went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while weeping, and the Messenger took it from them and said: "O Thawban, take this to the house of so-and-so, the people of a household in Medina, and buy for Fatima a necklace of ʿaṣab and two bracelets of ivory." He said: "Indeed these are the people of my household, and I do not wish that they should use up their good things in the life of this world." [5] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/275; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/43.]]

'Aqil ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed us: Muhammad ibn Jarir informed us: Kathir related to us: Yazid related to us: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, who said: a companion of ours related to us, from Abu Hurayra, who said: "Our food with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was only the two blacks: water and dates. By Allah, we did not see these your sumra (a kind of tree) and we did not know what they were."

And with the same chain, from Qatada, from Abu Burda ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qays al-Ash'ari, from his father, who said: "O my son, if you had witnessed us while we were with our Prophet (ﷺ), when the rain befell us, you would have thought our smell was the smell of sheep. Our clothing was only wool."

And with the same chain, from Qatada, who said: it has been mentioned to us that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say: "If I wished, I could be the best of you in food and the softest of you in clothing, but I hold back my good things." It was also mentioned to us that when he came to Syria, a meal was prepared for him the like of which he had never seen. He said: "This is for us. So what about the poor Muslims who died while they never had enough of barley bread?" Khalid ibn al-Walid said: "They have Paradise." 'Umar's eyes welled up with tears, and he said: "If our share is in the goods and they have departed, while in my view they are in Paradise, then indeed they have left us far behind."

It has also been mentioned to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon the People of the Suffa, a place where the poor Muslims gathered, and they were patching their garments with leather, finding no patches for them. He said: "Are you today better, or on a day when one of you goes out in one garment and comes back in another, and a bowl is brought to him in the morning and another in the evening, and he curtains his house as the Ka'ba is curtained?" They said: "We are better on that day."

Al-Husayn ibn Manjawayh informed us: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Nasrawayh related to us: Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Musa al-Jawhari related to us: 'Ali ibn Sahl al-Ramli related to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us: Razq Abu al-Hudhayl related to me: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah related to me, from Ibn 'Abbas, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), that he related to him that he entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he had abandoned his wives. He found him on a rough, rumpled bed, meaning a mat, a rope bed, the mat having left its mark on his side, reclining on a leather pillow stuffed with palm fiber.

'Umar said: "I looked around the room, and by Allah I did not see anything that would catch the eye except a hide, meaning a damaged skin, whose smell had spread. So I wept, and I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you are the Messenger of Allah and His chosen one, while, as I see it, Kisra and Caesar are in brocade and silk!'" Then the Messenger of Allah sat up and said: "Are you in doubt, O son of al-Khattab? Those are a people whose good things were hastened to them in their worldly life." [6] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/34.]]

Ibn Manjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Utba related to us: al-Furmani related to us: Abu Umayya al-Wasiti related to us: Yazid ibn Harun related to us: Mubarak ibn Fudala informed us: Hafs ibn Abi al-'As related to us, who said: "I used to have lunch with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and our lunch was bread with oil and vinegar, bread with milk, bread with dried meat, and the least of it was broad meat." He used to say: "Do not sift the flour, for all of it is food." [7]

Then he would bring thick, coarse bread, and he began to eat and said to us: "Eat!" So we began to make excuses, and he said: "What is the matter with you that you do not eat?" I said: "By Allah, O Commander of the Faithful, we do not eat it. We return to a food softer than your food."

He said: "Bah, O son of Abi al-'As! Do you not see that I know how to command that the flour be sifted with a cloth and baked in such and such a way? Do you not see that I know how to command that a fat kid goat be brought, its hair removed, and it come out roasted like such and such? Do you not see that I know how to command that a sa' or two sa's of raisins be made, placed in a waterskin, and water poured over them, and it is cooked until it becomes like the blood of a gazelle?"

He said: I said: "By Allah, O Commander of the Faithful, I see you as one who knows the pleasures of living well." 'Umar said: "Indeed, by Allah, besides whom there is no god, were it not that I fear my good deeds may be diminished on the Day of Resurrection, I would have shared with you in the living. But I heard Allah say concerning a people: ﴿You used up your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them﴾." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/624, no. 35924.]]

Ibn Manjawayh informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us: Muhammad ibn Bakkar al-Rayyan related to us: Abu Ma'shar related to us, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said:

My family craved meat, so I passed by 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), and he said: "What is this, O Jabir?" I said: "My family craved meat, so I bought meat for a dirham." He said: "Whenever one of you craves something, does he put it into his belly? Do you not fear that you may be among the people of this verse: ﴿You used up your good things in your worldly life﴾?"

Ibn Manjawayh informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us: Bishr related to us: Ibn Abi al-Khusayb related to us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Musa informed me: Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari related to us: my father related to us, who said: Wahb ibn al-Ward said: "The son of Adam was created with bread accompanying him, and whatever is added to bread increases appetite." He said: I related this to Abu Sulayman, and he said: "He is right. Salt with bread is a craving."

﴿And mention the brother of 'Ad﴾, meaning Hud (peace be upon him).

﴿when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: al-Ahqaf is a valley between 'Uman and Mahra. Muqatil said: the dwellings of 'Ad were in Yemen, in Hadramawt, at a place called Mahra, to which camels are attributed, so it is said: "Mahri camels" and "mahari" (she-camels). They were people of tents that moved about in spring, and when the pasture was lush, they returned to their dwellings. They were from the tribe of Iram.

Al-Dahhak said: al-Ahqaf is a mountain in Syria. Mujahid said: it is the land of Jasaq from Hismā. Qatada said: it has been mentioned to us that 'Ad were a people in Yemen, people of sand dunes overlooking the sea, in a land called al-Shihr. Ibn Zayd said: al-Ahqaf is what stretches of sand are like a mountain, without reaching the status of a mountain. [[See al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/43, at the verse.]]

Al-Kalbi said: al-Ahqaf is what the water receded from at the time of the flood, the water receding from the earth and leaving its trace. Al-Khalil said: they are great sand dunes. Al-Kisa'i said: they are sand that is curved, and its singular is ḥaqf and ḥiqāf, like dabagh and dibagh, and libs and libas. It was also said: ḥaqāf is the plural of ḥaqf, and aḥqāf is the plural of the plural.

The analogue of ḥaqf/aḥqāf is shabr/ashbār. Al-A'sha said:

"So he spent the night beside a tamarisk-covered dune, wrapped by a burning north wind that leaves the face ashen."

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/29.]]

And he said: "Between us a parched valley with winding dunes." It is said: ḥaqf, aḥqaf, meaning sand fully curved. Al-'Ajjaj said:

"He spent the night beside a tamarisk-covered dune, a dune bent."

Its verb is aḥqafa. The rajaz poet said:

"The crescent moon's edge until it bent."

That is, it inclined and curved.

﴿And warnings had already passed﴾, the messengers had passed on. ﴿from before him﴾, that is, before Hud, ﴿and from after him﴾, which in the reading of 'Abd Allah is "and after him." ﴿that you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great day.﴾ They said: ﴿"Have you come to us to turn us away﴾, to divert us ﴿from our gods? Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful."﴾ He said: ﴿"The knowledge is only with Allah﴾, of the time when the punishment will come, ﴿not with me, and I convey to you that with which I have been sent, but I see you as an ignorant people."﴾

﴿Then when they saw it﴾, meaning the punishment, ﴿as a cloud﴾, placed in the accusative as a circumstantial state; or if you wish, by repetition, meaning "they saw it as a cloud." It is the cloud, named so because it appears across the sky, meaning it shows itself on the breadth of the heavens.

Mujahid said: it swept them into the valley. Al-A'sha said:

"O you who see a cloud, I have spent the night watching it, as if lightning in its edges were torches."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/33.]]

The exegetes said: Allah drove the black cloud which Qayl ibn 'Anz had chosen, having returned with what it contained of vengeance to 'Ad, and it came out upon them from a valley of theirs called al-Mughith. They had been deprived of rain for days, so when they saw it...

[They said: "This is a cloud bringing us rain," until a woman among them named Mahdar recognized that it was a wind, and she cried out and fainted. When she recovered, it was said to her: "What did you see?" She said: "A wind in which were meteors of fire."] [[Tafsir al-Tha'alabi: 3/46 at the verse; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/235; Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/285.]]

﴿heading toward their valleys﴾, they rejoiced at it.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 46, verse 13–25 (part 2 of 2):

They said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Nay, it is that which you were seeking to hasten: a wind wherein is a painful punishment.﴾ So it began to carry off the tent and the litter-bearing camel, lifting them up until they appeared like locusts.

Ibn Manjuwayh informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah related to us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Kisa'i related to us: al-Harith ibn 'Abd Allah related to us: Hushaym related to us, from Juwaybir, who related to us: Abu Dawud al-A'ma, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿But when they saw it as a cloud coming toward their valleys﴾, to the end of the verse, he said:

When the cloud drew near, they stood up and stretched out their hands. The first thing by which they recognized that it was a punishment was that they saw what was outside their dwellings, their baggage and their livestock, being carried by the wind between the sky and the earth like the pigeons (rushā). They said: So they entered their houses and closed their doors. But the wind came, forced their doors open and threw them down. Allah commanded the wind, and it poured sand over them, so they were beneath the sand for seven nights and eight days, ﴿in succession, desolate﴾, groaning. Then Allah commanded the wind, and it removed the sand from them; then He commanded it, and it carried them away and cast them into the sea.

They are the ones of whom Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Destroying everything by the command of its Lord﴾ — it passed over the men of 'Ad and their wealth — ﴿by the permission of its Lord﴾.

Ibn Manjuwayh informed us: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl related to us: Abu Hisham related to us: Hafs related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to be alarmed when he saw the wind, and he would say: "O Allah, I ask You for its good, the good within it, and the good it has been sent with; and I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil within it, and the evil it has been sent with." [8] [[Sahih Muslim: 3/26; al-Sunan al-Kubra 3/360.]]

When he saw a sign of rain (mukhīlah), he would stand up, sit down, come and go, and his color would change. So we would say, "O Messenger of Allah, [why?]" He would say:
"I fear that it may be like the people of 'Ad, of whom they said: ﴿This is a cloud bringing us rain.﴾" [9] [[Ibid.]]

﴿So they became such that nothing was seen except their dwellings.﴾ Al-Hasan recited (لا تُرى) with a dammah on the tā' and إِلَّا مَساكِنُهُمْ with a raf' on the nūn. Similarly, Shu'ayb ibn Ayyub related it from Yahya ibn Adam, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, from 'Asim.

Abu Hatim said: This is not sound in the language unless one posits an implied elision (idmar), as you say in speech: "The women do not see except Zaynab," but you cannot say "does not see except Zaynab." Sibawayh said: its meaning is "(does not see) their persons" — إِلَّا مَساكِنُهُمْ. Al-Farra' considered this verse to be an irregular construction (istikrah), and he mentioned that al-Mufaddal recited to him:
"Our fire has not seen a fire like it; Ma'add knows this well, in generosity"
He made the verb feminine (fa-annatha fi'l mithl) because it refers to the fire. He said: The most eloquent speech would be to say: "Lam tara mithlaha nar" (no fire has seen the like of it). [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/36.]

Al-A'mash, 'Asim, Hamzah, Ya'qub and Khalaf recited (بياء) with a dammah on the yā', مَساكِنُهُمْ in the nominative, and Abu 'Ubaydah and Abu Hatim preferred the nominative. Al-Kisa'i said: its meaning is "nothing is seen except their dwellings."

Al-Farra' said: people are not seen because they were under the sand, so only their dwellings are seen, since they are standing.

The rest recited (تَرى) with a fatḥah on the tā' and (مساكنَهم) in the accusative, on the meaning: "you (O Muhammad) do not see except their dwellings."

﴿Thus do We recompense the guilty people.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 46, verses 13–25 (part 1 of 2)**

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve. Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein, as a reward for what they used to do.﴾ ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents.﴾ The common readers recite "ḥusnan" without an alif. The people of Kufa recite "iḥsanan," and this is the reading of Ibn 'Abbas. [[It is said that in the codices of the people of the two sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), Basra and Syria, the reading is "ḥusnan." Their proof is the words of the Exalted in Surat al-'Ankabut (29:8): ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Raja' recite "ḥasanan," with a fatḥa on the ḥa and the sīn. The proof of the common readers is the words of the Exalted in Surat al-An'am (6:151): ﴿and to parents, kindness﴾, and this is in the codices of the people of Kufa. (See Zad al-Masir: 6/121, and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/192.) I say: in the codices of the Muslims in this age the reading is "iḥsanan," and our proof is the words of the Exalted: ﴿and do not separate﴾.]]

﴿His mother bore him with hardship﴾, with difficulty and hardship. ﴿and she gave birth to him with hardship﴾, and ﴿his bearing and his weaning﴾, that is, his weaning from milk, ﴿is thirty months﴾. Al-Hasan and Ya'qub recite "wa-faṣluhu" without an alif. The exegetes said: his gestation was six months and his suckling was twenty-four months.

Ibn Ishaq said: his gestation was nine months and his weaning from milk was twenty-one months.

﴿Until, when he reaches his full strength﴾, the height of his power and stature and the peak of his youth and maturity, which is between eighteen and forty years of age. This is the meaning of His words, ﴿and reaches forty years﴾. Al-Suddi and al-Dahhak said: this verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. The story has already passed. Others said: it was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) and his father, Abu Quhafa 'Uthman ibn 'Amr, and his mother, Umm al-Khayr bint Sakhr ibn 'Amr ibn 'Amir. When Abu Bakr reached forty years, he believed in the Prophet (ﷺ) and said to his Lord: ﴿Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed I am among the Muslims.﴾

Ibn Manjawayh informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us: Ishaq ibn Sadaqa related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim related to us, from Sayf ibn 'Umar, from 'Atiyya, from Abu Ayyub, from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning His words: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾. It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr. Both of his parents embraced Islam, and no one among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah from among the Emigrants had both parents embrace Islam except him. Allah enjoined him concerning them, and this continued after him.

He said: ﴿My Lord, enable me﴾, inspire me and grant me capacity, ﴿to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness which You approve, and make righteous for me my offspring﴾, that You make them believing and righteous. They said: Allah answered Abu Bakr concerning his children, and they embraced Islam. No Companion other than Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) had himself, his parents, his sons and his daughters all embrace Islam.

﴿Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed I am among the Muslims.﴾ ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did﴾, meaning their righteous deeds, so He rewards them for them.

﴿And We overlook their misdeeds﴾, so He does not punish them for them. ﴿among the companions of Paradise﴾, that is, along with the companions of Paradise. The "fī" here means "with." ﴿the true promise which they were promised﴾, and it is His words: ﴿Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. [[Surat al-Tawba: 72.]]

﴿And he who says to his parents, when they call him to faith in Allah and affirmation of the Resurrection and the Recompense: "Uff to you both!"﴾ That is a word of aversion.

﴿"Do you promise me that I will be brought forth﴾ from my grave alive after my death and my decay?" The common readers recite "a-taʿidāninī" with two genuine nūns, while the people of Syria recite it with one doubled nūn. ﴿while generations have passed before me﴾, and none of them was resurrected. Al-Hasan, al-A'mash and Abu Ma'mar recite "an akhraja" with a fatḥa on the "rā'" and a ḍamma, [i.e., "an ukhraja" in the passive is read differently].

﴿And the two of them call upon Allah for help﴾, seeking His aid against him and saying to him: ﴿Woe to you! Believe, for indeed the promise of Allah is true.﴾ ﴿But he says, "This is not but the fables of the former peoples."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliya, al-Suddi and Mujahid said: this verse was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah. It was also said: it was revealed concerning 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq. His parents said to him: "Embrace Islam," and they insisted on calling him to faith. He said: "Bring back to life for me 'Abd Allah ibn Jud'an, 'Amir ibn Ka'b and the elders of Quraysh, so that I may ask them about what they say."

Muhammad ibn Ziyad said: Mu'awiya wrote to Marwan that the people should pledge allegiance to Yazid. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr said: "You have brought it as a Heraclian [monarchy], will you pledge allegiance to your sons?"

Marwan said: "This is the one about whom Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the one who says to his parents, 'Uff to you both! Do you promise me...﴾" to the end of the verse. 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her) heard of this and became angry, and she said: "By Allah, it is not about him. If I wished, I could name him, but Allah cursed your father while you were in his loins, so you are a son of the curse of Allah."

﴿Those are the ones against whom the word has come into effect﴾, meaning the punishment became obligatory for them. They said: that refers to those whom Ibn Abi Bakr indicated, and he said "bring them to me," and they are the ones against whom the word has come. They are the ones who passed away, as in His words: ﴿while generations have passed before me﴾. As for Ibn Abi Bakr, Allah answered his father's supplication in His words: ﴿and make righteous for me my offspring﴾, so he embraced Islam and his Islam was good.

Al-Hasan and Qatada said: this verse is general in its reference, and it describes a disbelieving, wicked servant who is disobedient to his parents. ﴿among nations﴾, along with nations ﴿which passed away before them, of jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers.﴾ ﴿And for each [of the two groups], the believers and the disbelievers, there are degrees﴾, ranks and levels with Allah on the Day of Resurrection according to their deeds, and He will recompense them for them. Ibn Zayd said: in this verse, the degrees of the people of the Fire go downward, and the degrees of the people of Paradise go upward.

﴿And that He may fully pay them their deeds﴾, their rewards, with the "yā'" (third person) read by Makki, Basri and Hisham, and the rest read it with the "nūn" (first person plural). ﴿and they will not be wronged.﴾

﴿And on the Day the disbelievers are exposed to the Fire﴾, it will be said to them: ﴿"You used up your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them﴾." Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir and Ya'qub recite "adhhabtum ṭayyibātikum" in the interrogative form, and it is differently reported from the people of Syria and others in the declarative form. Both are sound and eloquent, because the Arabs use the interrogative for reproach and omit the interrogative particle in it. So they say: "Did you go, and do such-and-such?" and "You went and did, and did?"

﴿So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you were arrogant about on earth without right, and for what you used to defy.﴾

Ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Manjawayh informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah related to us: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Karabisi related to us: Humayd ibn al-Rabi' related to us: Abu Ma'mar related to us: 'Abd al-Warith related to us: Muhammad ibn Hujara related to us, from Humayd al-Shami, from Sulayman, from Thawban, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Whenever the Messenger of Allah traveled, the last person he left was from his family, and the first person he entered upon when he returned was Fatima (peace be upon her)."

When he returned from a campaign and came to her, he glimpsed [something] at her door, and he saw on al-Hasan and al-Husayn two silver bracelets. So he turned back and did not enter upon her. When Fatima saw that, she thought he had not entered upon her because of what he had seen. So she tore the curtain and removed the two bracelets from the boys and cut them. The boys wept, so she divided it between them in two halves. They went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while weeping, and the Messenger took it from them and said: "O Thawban, take this to the house of so-and-so, the people of a household in Medina, and buy for Fatima a necklace of ʿaṣab and two bracelets of ivory." He said: "Indeed these are the people of my household, and I do not wish that they should use up their good things in the life of this world." [5] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/275; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/43.]]

'Aqil ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed us: Muhammad ibn Jarir informed us: Kathir related to us: Yazid related to us: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, who said: a companion of ours related to us, from Abu Hurayra, who said: "Our food with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was only the two blacks: water and dates. By Allah, we did not see these your sumra (a kind of tree) and we did not know what they were."

And with the same chain, from Qatada, from Abu Burda ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qays al-Ash'ari, from his father, who said: "O my son, if you had witnessed us while we were with our Prophet (ﷺ), when the rain befell us, you would have thought our smell was the smell of sheep. Our clothing was only wool."

And with the same chain, from Qatada, who said: it has been mentioned to us that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say: "If I wished, I could be the best of you in food and the softest of you in clothing, but I hold back my good things." It was also mentioned to us that when he came to Syria, a meal was prepared for him the like of which he had never seen. He said: "This is for us. So what about the poor Muslims who died while they never had enough of barley bread?" Khalid ibn al-Walid said: "They have Paradise." 'Umar's eyes welled up with tears, and he said: "If our share is in the goods and they have departed, while in my view they are in Paradise, then indeed they have left us far behind."

It has also been mentioned to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon the People of the Suffa, a place where the poor Muslims gathered, and they were patching their garments with leather, finding no patches for them. He said: "Are you today better, or on a day when one of you goes out in one garment and comes back in another, and a bowl is brought to him in the morning and another in the evening, and he curtains his house as the Ka'ba is curtained?" They said: "We are better on that day."

Al-Husayn ibn Manjawayh informed us: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Nasrawayh related to us: Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Musa al-Jawhari related to us: 'Ali ibn Sahl al-Ramli related to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us: Razq Abu al-Hudhayl related to me: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah related to me, from Ibn 'Abbas, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), that he related to him that he entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he had abandoned his wives. He found him on a rough, rumpled bed, meaning a mat, a rope bed, the mat having left its mark on his side, reclining on a leather pillow stuffed with palm fiber.

'Umar said: "I looked around the room, and by Allah I did not see anything that would catch the eye except a hide, meaning a damaged skin, whose smell had spread. So I wept, and I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you are the Messenger of Allah and His chosen one, while, as I see it, Kisra and Caesar are in brocade and silk!'" Then the Messenger of Allah sat up and said: "Are you in doubt, O son of al-Khattab? Those are a people whose good things were hastened to them in their worldly life." [6] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/34.]]

Ibn Manjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Utba related to us: al-Furmani related to us: Abu Umayya al-Wasiti related to us: Yazid ibn Harun related to us: Mubarak ibn Fudala informed us: Hafs ibn Abi al-'As related to us, who said: "I used to have lunch with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and our lunch was bread with oil and vinegar, bread with milk, bread with dried meat, and the least of it was broad meat." He used to say: "Do not sift the flour, for all of it is food." [7]

Then he would bring thick, coarse bread, and he began to eat and said to us: "Eat!" So we began to make excuses, and he said: "What is the matter with you that you do not eat?" I said: "By Allah, O Commander of the Faithful, we do not eat it. We return to a food softer than your food."

He said: "Bah, O son of Abi al-'As! Do you not see that I know how to command that the flour be sifted with a cloth and baked in such and such a way? Do you not see that I know how to command that a fat kid goat be brought, its hair removed, and it come out roasted like such and such? Do you not see that I know how to command that a sa' or two sa's of raisins be made, placed in a waterskin, and water poured over them, and it is cooked until it becomes like the blood of a gazelle?"

He said: I said: "By Allah, O Commander of the Faithful, I see you as one who knows the pleasures of living well." 'Umar said: "Indeed, by Allah, besides whom there is no god, were it not that I fear my good deeds may be diminished on the Day of Resurrection, I would have shared with you in the living. But I heard Allah say concerning a people: ﴿You used up your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them﴾." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/624, no. 35924.]]

Ibn Manjawayh informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us: Muhammad ibn Bakkar al-Rayyan related to us: Abu Ma'shar related to us, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said:

My family craved meat, so I passed by 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), and he said: "What is this, O Jabir?" I said: "My family craved meat, so I bought meat for a dirham." He said: "Whenever one of you craves something, does he put it into his belly? Do you not fear that you may be among the people of this verse: ﴿You used up your good things in your worldly life﴾?"

Ibn Manjawayh informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us: Bishr related to us: Ibn Abi al-Khusayb related to us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Musa informed me: Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari related to us: my father related to us, who said: Wahb ibn al-Ward said: "The son of Adam was created with bread accompanying him, and whatever is added to bread increases appetite." He said: I related this to Abu Sulayman, and he said: "He is right. Salt with bread is a craving."

﴿And mention the brother of 'Ad﴾, meaning Hud (peace be upon him).

﴿when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: al-Ahqaf is a valley between 'Uman and Mahra. Muqatil said: the dwellings of 'Ad were in Yemen, in Hadramawt, at a place called Mahra, to which camels are attributed, so it is said: "Mahri camels" and "mahari" (she-camels). They were people of tents that moved about in spring, and when the pasture was lush, they returned to their dwellings. They were from the tribe of Iram.

Al-Dahhak said: al-Ahqaf is a mountain in Syria. Mujahid said: it is the land of Jasaq from Hismā. Qatada said: it has been mentioned to us that 'Ad were a people in Yemen, people of sand dunes overlooking the sea, in a land called al-Shihr. Ibn Zayd said: al-Ahqaf is what stretches of sand are like a mountain, without reaching the status of a mountain. [[See al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/43, at the verse.]]

Al-Kalbi said: al-Ahqaf is what the water receded from at the time of the flood, the water receding from the earth and leaving its trace. Al-Khalil said: they are great sand dunes. Al-Kisa'i said: they are sand that is curved, and its singular is ḥaqf and ḥiqāf, like dabagh and dibagh, and libs and libas. It was also said: ḥaqāf is the plural of ḥaqf, and aḥqāf is the plural of the plural.

The analogue of ḥaqf/aḥqāf is shabr/ashbār. Al-A'sha said:

"So he spent the night beside a tamarisk-covered dune, wrapped by a burning north wind that leaves the face ashen."

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/29.]]

And he said: "Between us a parched valley with winding dunes." It is said: ḥaqf, aḥqaf, meaning sand fully curved. Al-'Ajjaj said:

"He spent the night beside a tamarisk-covered dune, a dune bent."

Its verb is aḥqafa. The rajaz poet said:

"The crescent moon's edge until it bent."

That is, it inclined and curved.

﴿And warnings had already passed﴾, the messengers had passed on. ﴿from before him﴾, that is, before Hud, ﴿and from after him﴾, which in the reading of 'Abd Allah is "and after him." ﴿that you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great day.﴾ They said: ﴿"Have you come to us to turn us away﴾, to divert us ﴿from our gods? Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful."﴾ He said: ﴿"The knowledge is only with Allah﴾, of the time when the punishment will come, ﴿not with me, and I convey to you that with which I have been sent, but I see you as an ignorant people."﴾

﴿Then when they saw it﴾, meaning the punishment, ﴿as a cloud﴾, placed in the accusative as a circumstantial state; or if you wish, by repetition, meaning "they saw it as a cloud." It is the cloud, named so because it appears across the sky, meaning it shows itself on the breadth of the heavens.

Mujahid said: it swept them into the valley. Al-A'sha said:

"O you who see a cloud, I have spent the night watching it, as if lightning in its edges were torches."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/33.]]

The exegetes said: Allah drove the black cloud which Qayl ibn 'Anz had chosen, having returned with what it contained of vengeance to 'Ad, and it came out upon them from a valley of theirs called al-Mughith. They had been deprived of rain for days, so when they saw it...

[They said: "This is a cloud bringing us rain," until a woman among them named Mahdar recognized that it was a wind, and she cried out and fainted. When she recovered, it was said to her: "What did you see?" She said: "A wind in which were meteors of fire."] [[Tafsir al-Tha'alabi: 3/46 at the verse; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/235; Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/285.]]

﴿heading toward their valleys﴾, they rejoiced at it.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 46, verse 13–25 (part 2 of 2):

They said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Nay, it is that which you were seeking to hasten: a wind wherein is a painful punishment.﴾ So it began to carry off the tent and the litter-bearing camel, lifting them up until they appeared like locusts.

Ibn Manjuwayh informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah related to us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Kisa'i related to us: al-Harith ibn 'Abd Allah related to us: Hushaym related to us, from Juwaybir, who related to us: Abu Dawud al-A'ma, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿But when they saw it as a cloud coming toward their valleys﴾, to the end of the verse, he said:

When the cloud drew near, they stood up and stretched out their hands. The first thing by which they recognized that it was a punishment was that they saw what was outside their dwellings, their baggage and their livestock, being carried by the wind between the sky and the earth like the pigeons (rushā). They said: So they entered their houses and closed their doors. But the wind came, forced their doors open and threw them down. Allah commanded the wind, and it poured sand over them, so they were beneath the sand for seven nights and eight days, ﴿in succession, desolate﴾, groaning. Then Allah commanded the wind, and it removed the sand from them; then He commanded it, and it carried them away and cast them into the sea.

They are the ones of whom Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Destroying everything by the command of its Lord﴾ — it passed over the men of 'Ad and their wealth — ﴿by the permission of its Lord﴾.

Ibn Manjuwayh informed us: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl related to us: Abu Hisham related to us: Hafs related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to be alarmed when he saw the wind, and he would say: "O Allah, I ask You for its good, the good within it, and the good it has been sent with; and I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil within it, and the evil it has been sent with." [8] [[Sahih Muslim: 3/26; al-Sunan al-Kubra 3/360.]]

When he saw a sign of rain (mukhīlah), he would stand up, sit down, come and go, and his color would change. So we would say, "O Messenger of Allah, [why?]" He would say:
"I fear that it may be like the people of 'Ad, of whom they said: ﴿This is a cloud bringing us rain.﴾" [9] [[Ibid.]]

﴿So they became such that nothing was seen except their dwellings.﴾ Al-Hasan recited (لا تُرى) with a dammah on the tā' and إِلَّا مَساكِنُهُمْ with a raf' on the nūn. Similarly, Shu'ayb ibn Ayyub related it from Yahya ibn Adam, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, from 'Asim.

Abu Hatim said: This is not sound in the language unless one posits an implied elision (idmar), as you say in speech: "The women do not see except Zaynab," but you cannot say "does not see except Zaynab." Sibawayh said: its meaning is "(does not see) their persons" — إِلَّا مَساكِنُهُمْ. Al-Farra' considered this verse to be an irregular construction (istikrah), and he mentioned that al-Mufaddal recited to him:
"Our fire has not seen a fire like it; Ma'add knows this well, in generosity"
He made the verb feminine (fa-annatha fi'l mithl) because it refers to the fire. He said: The most eloquent speech would be to say: "Lam tara mithlaha nar" (no fire has seen the like of it). [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/36.]

Al-A'mash, 'Asim, Hamzah, Ya'qub and Khalaf recited (بياء) with a dammah on the yā', مَساكِنُهُمْ in the nominative, and Abu 'Ubaydah and Abu Hatim preferred the nominative. Al-Kisa'i said: its meaning is "nothing is seen except their dwellings."

Al-Farra' said: people are not seen because they were under the sand, so only their dwellings are seen, since they are standing.

The rest recited (تَرى) with a fatḥah on the tā' and (مساكنَهم) in the accusative, on the meaning: "you (O Muhammad) do not see except their dwellings."

﴿Thus do We recompense the guilty people.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 46, verses 13–25 (part 1 of 2)**

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve. Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein, as a reward for what they used to do.﴾ ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents.﴾ The common readers recite "ḥusnan" without an alif. The people of Kufa recite "iḥsanan," and this is the reading of Ibn 'Abbas. [[It is said that in the codices of the people of the two sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), Basra and Syria, the reading is "ḥusnan." Their proof is the words of the Exalted in Surat al-'Ankabut (29:8): ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Raja' recite "ḥasanan," with a fatḥa on the ḥa and the sīn. The proof of the common readers is the words of the Exalted in Surat al-An'am (6:151): ﴿and to parents, kindness﴾, and this is in the codices of the people of Kufa. (See Zad al-Masir: 6/121, and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/192.) I say: in the codices of the Muslims in this age the reading is "iḥsanan," and our proof is the words of the Exalted: ﴿and do not separate﴾.]]

﴿His mother bore him with hardship﴾, with difficulty and hardship. ﴿and she gave birth to him with hardship﴾, and ﴿his bearing and his weaning﴾, that is, his weaning from milk, ﴿is thirty months﴾. Al-Hasan and Ya'qub recite "wa-faṣluhu" without an alif. The exegetes said: his gestation was six months and his suckling was twenty-four months.

Ibn Ishaq said: his gestation was nine months and his weaning from milk was twenty-one months.

﴿Until, when he reaches his full strength﴾, the height of his power and stature and the peak of his youth and maturity, which is between eighteen and forty years of age. This is the meaning of His words, ﴿and reaches forty years﴾. Al-Suddi and al-Dahhak said: this verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. The story has already passed. Others said: it was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) and his father, Abu Quhafa 'Uthman ibn 'Amr, and his mother, Umm al-Khayr bint Sakhr ibn 'Amr ibn 'Amir. When Abu Bakr reached forty years, he believed in the Prophet (ﷺ) and said to his Lord: ﴿Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed I am among the Muslims.﴾

Ibn Manjawayh informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us: Ishaq ibn Sadaqa related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim related to us, from Sayf ibn 'Umar, from 'Atiyya, from Abu Ayyub, from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning His words: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾. It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr. Both of his parents embraced Islam, and no one among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah from among the Emigrants had both parents embrace Islam except him. Allah enjoined him concerning them, and this continued after him.
