When the Messenger of God was at ease, he said: "O God, I complain to You of the weakness of my strength, the scarcity of my resources, and my insignificance before people. O Most Merciful of the merciful, You are the Lord of the weak, and You are my Lord. To whom will You entrust me? To a distant one who scowls at me, or to an enemy You have given power over my affair? If You are not angry with me, I do not mind; but Your well-being is wider for me. I seek refuge in the light of Your Face from Your wrath descending upon me or Your displeasure befalling me. To You belongs the reproof until You are pleased. There is no might nor power except in You."

When the sons of Rabi'ah saw what had befallen him, their kinship moved them. They called a Christian slave of theirs named ʿAddas, and said to him: "Take a bunch of this grape and put it on that platter, then go with it to that man and tell him to eat from it." ʿAddas did so, then came with it and placed it before the Messenger of God (ﷺ). When the Messenger of God put forth his hand, he said: "In the name of God."

Then he ate. ʿAddas looked at his face and said: "By God, this is not what the people of this land say."

The Messenger of God said to him: "From which people of the lands are you, O ʿAddas? And what is your religion?" He said: "I am a Christian, and I am a man from the people of Nineveh."

The Messenger of God said to him: "From the town of the righteous man, Yunus ibn Matta." He said to him: "And what would you know of Yunus ibn Matta?!" The Messenger of God said: "He is my brother; he was a prophet, and I am a prophet." Then ʿAddas bent over the Messenger of God (ﷺ), kissed his head, his hands, and his feet.

He said: The sons of Rabi'ah said to one another: "As for your slave, he has corrupted him for you." When ʿAddas came to them, they said to him: "Woe to you, ʿAddas! What is it with you that you kiss this man's head, his hands, and his feet?!" He said: "O my master, there is nothing on earth better than this man. He has informed me of a matter which none knows except a prophet." They said: "Woe to you, ʿAddas! Do not let him turn you away from your religion, for your religion is better than his."

Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) departed from al-Ta'if, returning to Makkah, having despaired of any good from Thaqif. When he reached Nakhlah, he rose in the depths of the night to pray. A group of jinn from the people of Nasibin in Yemen passed by him. The reason for this was that the jinn used to steal listening to the heavens, but when the sky was guarded and they were pelted with shooting stars, Iblis said: "What has happened in the sky must be for something on the earth." So he dispatched his troops to find out the news. The first expedition he sent was a company from the people of Nasibin, who were the nobles and leaders of the jinn. He sent them to Tihamah, and they set out until they reached the valley of Nakhlah, where they found the Messenger of God (ﷺ) praying the dawn prayer in the hollow of Nakhlah, reciting the Qur'an. They listened to him, and said: ﴿Be silent!﴾

This is the meaning of the statement of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and a group of the leading narrators, and the narration of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Others said: Rather, the Messenger of God was commanded to warn the jinn, invite them to God Most High, and recite the Qur'an to them. So God turned to him a company of jinn from Nineveh and gathered them for him. The Messenger of God said: "I have been commanded to recite the Qur'an to the jinn tonight, so which of you will follow me?" They lowered their heads. He asked them again, and they lowered their heads. Then he asked them a third time, and ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud followed him. ʿAbd Allah said: No one else was present with him but me. We set out until, when we were at the upper part of Makkah, the Prophet of God (ﷺ) entered a mountain pass called Shiʿb al-Hajun, and drew a line for me, then commanded me to sit within it.

He said: "Do not leave it until I return to you." Then he went off until he stood and began the Qur'an. I began to see things like vultures swooping, walking in their wings, and I heard a great commotion, until I feared for the Prophet of God. A large number of black shapes came between me and him, until I could no longer hear his voice. Then they began to disperse like pieces of cloud, scattered. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) came to me at dawn, and said: "Have you slept?" I said: "No, by God, I was determined many times to call for help from the people, until I heard you rebuking them with your staff, saying: 'Sit down!'"

He said: "Had you come out, I would not have been safe that some of them might snatch you away."

Then he said: "Did you see anything?" I said: "Yes, I saw men, black, wearing white garments." He said: "Those were the jinn of Nasibin, who asked me for provisions" — and provisions means food — "so I provided them with every bone that is dry and every dung and dropping." They said: "O Messenger of God, people will consider it filth for us." So the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade cleaning oneself with bones and dung.

He said: I said: "O Messenger of God, what does that benefit them?" He said: "They do not find a bone but that they find meat on it, the day it was eaten, and no dropping but that they find in it its grain, the day you ate."

I said: "O Messenger of God, there was a great commotion." He said: "The jinn were arguing over a slain man who was killed among them" — and it was said: "killed" — "so they came to me for judgment, and I judged between them with truth." He said: Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) relieved himself, then came to me and said: "Do you have water with you?" I said: "O Messenger of God, I have a waterskin with some date nabidh in it." He asked for it, and I poured it over his hands, and he performed ablution.

He said: "A good date and pure water." Qatadah said: Ibn Mas'ud told us that when he came to Kufah, he saw some grey-haired elders of the Zutt, and they frightened him when he saw them. He said: "Show yourselves!" It was said to him: "These are a people of the Zutt." He said: "How alike they are to the company who were turned towards the Messenger of God (ﷺ)," meaning the jinn. [[Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 6/169.]]

He said: Ibn Manjuwayh informed me: Ibn Hanash al-Muqri narrated to us, Ibn Zanjuwayh narrated to us, Salamah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Mu'ammar narrated to us, from Qatadah, with the like of its meaning, except that he did not mention the story of the date nabidh.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hadithi informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi narrated to us, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Dhurayh narrated to us, Masruq ibn al-Marzuban narrated to us, Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from ʿAlqamah, who said: I asked ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud: "Was there anyone with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) from the jinn?"

He said: "No, none of us accompanied him. But we lost him one night, and we said: 'He has been carried off or seized.' We scattered through the mountain passes and valleys seeking him. When we woke in the morning, we saw him coming from the direction of Hira."

We said: "O Messenger of God, we spent the worst night any people ever spent, saying: 'He has been carried off or seized.'"

He said: "A summoner from the jinn came to me, and I went to recite the Qur'an to them." He said: And he showed me their traces and the traces of their fires. He said: "They asked him that night for provisions."

He said: "Every bone over which the name of God has not been mentioned that falls into your hands will be fuller with meat than it was, and dung will be fodder for your animals."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Do not cleanse yourselves with bones or dung, for they are the provision of your brothers from the jinn." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 1/16.]]

Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn Manjuwayh informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Kharijah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ayyub narrated to us, Salman ibn Dawud al-Shadhkuni informed us, from Khalid ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Wasiti, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: "I was not with the Prophet (ﷺ) on the night of the jinn, and I wished I had been with him."

Ibn Manjuwayh informed us: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAli narrated to us, Yusuf ibn Ya'qub al-Qadi narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, who said: I asked Abu ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allah: "Was ʿAbd Allah with the Prophet (ﷺ) on the night of the jinn?" He said: "No." He said: I asked Ibrahim, and he said: "I wish our companion had been there."

The words of God Most High: ﴿And when We turned towards you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an﴾. They differed concerning their number. Ibn ʿAbbas said: They were seven men from the jinn of Nasibin, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) made them messengers to their people.

Ibn Manjuwayh informed us: Talhah ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far and ʿUbayd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, both saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid informed us, Ahmad ibn Harb narrated to me, Sunayd narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, who said: Ibn Jurayj said: Wahb ibn Sulayman informed me, from Shu'ayb al-Hummani: that the names of the jinn whom God Most High turned to His Messenger were Shasir, Masir, Mansha, Mashi, and al-Ahqab. [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/214 and Fath al-Bari: 8/517.]] Others said they were nine.

Abu ʿAli al-Sarraj informed me: Abu Bakr al-Qattan narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firyabi narrated to us, who said: Sufyan mentioned, from ʿAsim, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: Zawba'ah was among the nine who listened to the Qur'an from the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿So when they came into its presence, they said: "Be silent!"﴾ They said: "Sh!" And with his chain, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Thabit ibn Qutbah al-Thaqafi, who said: Some people came to ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud and said: "We were on a journey and saw a snake, writhing in its blood, killed. One of us took it, and we buried it. When they turned away, some people came to them and said: 'You have buried ʿAmr!' They said: 'And who is ʿAmr?' They said: 'The snake you buried in such-and-such a place.' Indeed he was one of the company who listened to the Qur'an from the Prophet (ﷺ), and between two snakes of the jinn, from among the Muslims and others, there was enmity, and he was killed."

Ibn Manjuwayh informed us: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab narrated to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, Sahl ibn Hamzah narrated to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Abu al-Zahiriyyah, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The jinn are of three kinds: one kind has wings and flies in the air; a second kind are snakes and dogs; and a third kind settle and move about." [[Mustadrak al-Hakim: 2/456.]]

﴿So when they came into its presence, they said﴾, that is, some of them said to others: "Be silent!" So they were silent and listened to the Qur'an, until some of them nearly fell upon others from the intensity of their eagerness, similar to what is in Surat al-Jinn.

﴿So when it was finished﴾, that is, when he had finished reciting the Qur'an and the jinn had finished listening. Luhaq ibn Hamid read "qada" with a fatha on the qaf and the dad, meaning the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿they turned back to their people as warners﴾, warning and calling them by the command of the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿They said: "O our people, we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what came before it, guiding to the truth and to a straight path. O our people, respond to the summoner of God﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ),

﴿and believe in him; He will forgive you some of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: So there answered them from above them about seventy men from the jinn, and they returned to the Messenger of God and met him at al-Batha'. He recited the Qur'an to them, and commanded and forbade them. The scholars differed concerning the ruling on believing jinn. Some said: The believing jinn have no reward except being saved from the Fire, and they interpreted His saying: ﴿He will forgive you some of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.﴾ This was the view of Abu Hanifah.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Manjuwayh informed us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Najawayh narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Thawr and Ibrahim ibn Abi Sufyan narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Farbani narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, who said: The reward of the jinn is that they are protected from the Fire, then it is said to them: "Be dust, like the beasts."

Others said: If they bear punishment for wrongdoing, it is necessary that they receive reward for good deeds, just like humans. This was the view of Malik and Ibn Abi Layla.

Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Thaqafi al-Dinawari informed us: Abu ʿAli ibn Habash al-Muqri narrated to us, Muhammad ibn ʿImran narrated to us, Ibn al-Muqri and Abu ʿUbayd Allah narrated to us, both saying: al-ʿAbdi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: The jinn enter Paradise and eat and drink.

﴿And whoever does not respond to the summoner of God, he cannot escape on earth, and he has no protectors besides Him. Those are in manifest error.﴾

﴿And We had established them in that wherein We have not established you,﴾ that is, in that which you cannot attain: bodily stature, physical strength, long life, and abundant wealth.

﴿And We made for them hearing and sight and hearts, but their hearing and their sight and their hearts availed them nothing at all, since they used to deny the signs of God, and there befell them what they used to mock.﴾ ﴿And We destroyed the towns around you﴾, O people of Makkah,

﴿from the towns﴾, such as the rock-dwelling of Thamud, the land of Sodom, and their like.

﴿And We varied the signs﴾, the proofs, clear evidences, and various kinds of lessons and admonitions, ﴿that they might return﴾ from their disbelief. But they did not return, so We destroyed them. (This is) a warning to the idolaters of Quraysh.

﴿Why then did those whom they took as gods besides God, as an offering, not help them?﴾ Meaning the idols. Al-Kisa'i said: "The qurban (offering) is everything by which one draws near to God Most High through obedience and sacrifice, and its plural is qarabin, like rahban and rahabin."

﴿Rather, they vanished from them. That was their falsehood﴾, that is, their lie, which they used to say: that these would bring them near to God Most High and intercede for them with Him. Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn al-Zubayr read "dhālika ifakahum" with a fatha on the alif and the fa, as a verb, meaning: that statement turned them away from monotheism. ʿIkrima read "ifakahum" with a shaddah on the fa, for emphasis and explanation. Abu Hatim said: it means that it turned their hearts away from the blessings they had been enjoying. The evidence for the reading of the majority is His saying: ﴿and what they used to fabricate.﴾

﴿And when We turned towards you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an…﴾ (the verse).

The exegetes said: When Abu Talib died, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) went out alone to al-Ta'if, seeking the support of Thaqif and protection from his people.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) reached al-Ta'if alone, he went to a group of Thaqif, who were then the leaders and nobles of Thaqif, and they were three brothers: ʿAbd Yalil, Mas'ud, and Habib, sons of ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr. With them was a woman from Quraysh from the Banu Jumah. He sat with them, invited them to God Most High, and spoke to them about what he had come with, seeking their support for Islam and their standing with him against those of his people who opposed him.

One of them said: "I will tear the garments of the Ka'bah if God sent you." Another said: "Could God not find anyone else to send but you?" The third said: "By God, I will never speak to you a single word. If you are truly a messenger from God as you say, then you are too great a matter for me to answer you; and if you are lying about God, then it is not fitting for me to speak with you."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) rose from them, having despaired of any good from Thaqif, and said to them: "When you have done what you have done, then keep it secret."

The Messenger of God disliked that they should report about him to his people, lest they turn them against him over this. But they did not do so; they incited their foolish ones and their slaves against him, who insulted him and shouted at him, until the people gathered around him and drove him to a garden wall belonging to ʿUtbah and Shaybah, the sons of Rabi'ah, and he took refuge there. The foolish ones of Thaqif turned back from him.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) met that woman from the Banu Jumah, and said to her: "What did we encounter from your in-laws?"

When the Messenger of God was at ease, he said: "O God, I complain to You of the weakness of my strength, the scarcity of my resources, and my insignificance before people. O Most Merciful of the merciful, You are the Lord of the weak, and You are my Lord. To whom will You entrust me? To a distant one who scowls at me, or to an enemy You have given power over my affair? If You are not angry with me, I do not mind; but Your well-being is wider for me. I seek refuge in the light of Your Face from Your wrath descending upon me or Your displeasure befalling me. To You belongs the reproof until You are pleased. There is no might nor power except in You."

When the sons of Rabi'ah saw what had befallen him, their kinship moved them. They called a Christian slave of theirs named ʿAddas, and said to him: "Take a bunch of this grape and put it on that platter, then go with it to that man and tell him to eat from it." ʿAddas did so, then came with it and placed it before the Messenger of God (ﷺ). When the Messenger of God put forth his hand, he said: "In the name of God."

Then he ate. ʿAddas looked at his face and said: "By God, this is not what the people of this land say."

The Messenger of God said to him: "From which people of the lands are you, O ʿAddas? And what is your religion?" He said: "I am a Christian, and I am a man from the people of Nineveh."

The Messenger of God said to him: "From the town of the righteous man, Yunus ibn Matta." He said to him: "And what would you know of Yunus ibn Matta?!" The Messenger of God said: "He is my brother; he was a prophet, and I am a prophet." Then ʿAddas bent over the Messenger of God (ﷺ), kissed his head, his hands, and his feet.

He said: The sons of Rabi'ah said to one another: "As for your slave, he has corrupted him for you." When ʿAddas came to them, they said to him: "Woe to you, ʿAddas! What is it with you that you kiss this man's head, his hands, and his feet?!" He said: "O my master, there is nothing on earth better than this man. He has informed me of a matter which none knows except a prophet." They said: "Woe to you, ʿAddas! Do not let him turn you away from your religion, for your religion is better than his."

Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) departed from al-Ta'if, returning to Makkah, having despaired of any good from Thaqif. When he reached Nakhlah, he rose in the depths of the night to pray. A group of jinn from the people of Nasibin in Yemen passed by him. The reason for this was that the jinn used to steal listening to the heavens, but when the sky was guarded and they were pelted with shooting stars, Iblis said: "What has happened in the sky must be for something on the earth." So he dispatched his troops to find out the news. The first expedition he sent was a company from the people of Nasibin, who were the nobles and leaders of the jinn. He sent them to Tihamah, and they set out until they reached the valley of Nakhlah, where they found the Messenger of God (ﷺ) praying the dawn prayer in the hollow of Nakhlah, reciting the Qur'an. They listened to him, and said: ﴿Be silent!﴾

This is the meaning of the statement of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and a group of the leading narrators, and the narration of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Others said: Rather, the Messenger of God was commanded to warn the jinn, invite them to God Most High, and recite the Qur'an to them. So God turned to him a company of jinn from Nineveh and gathered them for him. The Messenger of God said: "I have been commanded to recite the Qur'an to the jinn tonight, so which of you will follow me?" They lowered their heads. He asked them again, and they lowered their heads. Then he asked them a third time, and ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud followed him. ʿAbd Allah said: No one else was present with him but me. We set out until, when we were at the upper part of Makkah, the Prophet of God (ﷺ) entered a mountain pass called Shiʿb al-Hajun, and drew a line for me, then commanded me to sit within it.

He said: "Do not leave it until I return to you." Then he went off until he stood and began the Qur'an. I began to see things like vultures swooping, walking in their wings, and I heard a great commotion, until I feared for the Prophet of God. A large number of black shapes came between me and him, until I could no longer hear his voice. Then they began to disperse like pieces of cloud, scattered. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) came to me at dawn, and said: "Have you slept?" I said: "No, by God, I was determined many times to call for help from the people, until I heard you rebuking them with your staff, saying: 'Sit down!'"

He said: "Had you come out, I would not have been safe that some of them might snatch you away."

Then he said: "Did you see anything?" I said: "Yes, I saw men, black, wearing white garments." He said: "Those were the jinn of Nasibin, who asked me for provisions" — and provisions means food — "so I provided them with every bone that is dry and every dung and dropping." They said: "O Messenger of God, people will consider it filth for us." So the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade cleaning oneself with bones and dung.

He said: I said: "O Messenger of God, what does that benefit them?" He said: "They do not find a bone but that they find meat on it, the day it was eaten, and no dropping but that they find in it its grain, the day you ate."

I said: "O Messenger of God, there was a great commotion." He said: "The jinn were arguing over a slain man who was killed among them" — and it was said: "killed" — "so they came to me for judgment, and I judged between them with truth." He said: Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) relieved himself, then came to me and said: "Do you have water with you?" I said: "O Messenger of God, I have a waterskin with some date nabidh in it." He asked for it, and I poured it over his hands, and he performed ablution.

He said: "A good date and pure water." Qatadah said: Ibn Mas'ud told us that when he came to Kufah, he saw some grey-haired elders of the Zutt, and they frightened him when he saw them. He said: "Show yourselves!" It was said to him: "These are a people of the Zutt." He said: "How alike they are to the company who were turned towards the Messenger of God (ﷺ)," meaning the jinn. [[Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 6/169.]]

He said: Ibn Manjuwayh informed me: Ibn Hanash al-Muqri narrated to us, Ibn Zanjuwayh narrated to us, Salamah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Mu'ammar narrated to us, from Qatadah, with the like of its meaning, except that he did not mention the story of the date nabidh.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hadithi informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi narrated to us, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Dhurayh narrated to us, Masruq ibn al-Marzuban narrated to us, Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from ʿAlqamah, who said: I asked ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud: "Was there anyone with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) from the jinn?"

He said: "No, none of us accompanied him. But we lost him one night, and we said: 'He has been carried off or seized.' We scattered through the mountain passes and valleys seeking him. When we woke in the morning, we saw him coming from the direction of Hira."

We said: "O Messenger of God, we spent the worst night any people ever spent, saying: 'He has been carried off or seized.'"

He said: "A summoner from the jinn came to me, and I went to recite the Qur'an to them." He said: And he showed me their traces and the traces of their fires. He said: "They asked him that night for provisions."

He said: "Every bone over which the name of God has not been mentioned that falls into your hands will be fuller with meat than it was, and dung will be fodder for your animals."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Do not cleanse yourselves with bones or dung, for they are the provision of your brothers from the jinn." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 1/16.]]

Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn Manjuwayh informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Kharijah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ayyub narrated to us, Salman ibn Dawud al-Shadhkuni informed us, from Khalid ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Wasiti, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: "I was not with the Prophet (ﷺ) on the night of the jinn, and I wished I had been with him."

Ibn Manjuwayh informed us: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAli narrated to us, Yusuf ibn Ya'qub al-Qadi narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, who said: I asked Abu ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allah: "Was ʿAbd Allah with the Prophet (ﷺ) on the night of the jinn?" He said: "No." He said: I asked Ibrahim, and he said: "I wish our companion had been there."

The words of God Most High: ﴿And when We turned towards you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an﴾. They differed concerning their number. Ibn ʿAbbas said: They were seven men from the jinn of Nasibin, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) made them messengers to their people.

Ibn Manjuwayh informed us: Talhah ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far and ʿUbayd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, both saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid informed us, Ahmad ibn Harb narrated to me, Sunayd narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, who said: Ibn Jurayj said: Wahb ibn Sulayman informed me, from Shu'ayb al-Hummani: that the names of the jinn whom God Most High turned to His Messenger were Shasir, Masir, Mansha, Mashi, and al-Ahqab. [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/214 and Fath al-Bari: 8/517.]] Others said they were nine.

Abu ʿAli al-Sarraj informed me: Abu Bakr al-Qattan narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firyabi narrated to us, who said: Sufyan mentioned, from ʿAsim, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: Zawba'ah was among the nine who listened to the Qur'an from the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿So when they came into its presence, they said: "Be silent!"﴾ They said: "Sh!" And with his chain, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Thabit ibn Qutbah al-Thaqafi, who said: Some people came to ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud and said: "We were on a journey and saw a snake, writhing in its blood, killed. One of us took it, and we buried it. When they turned away, some people came to them and said: 'You have buried ʿAmr!' They said: 'And who is ʿAmr?' They said: 'The snake you buried in such-and-such a place.' Indeed he was one of the company who listened to the Qur'an from the Prophet (ﷺ), and between two snakes of the jinn, from among the Muslims and others, there was enmity, and he was killed."

Ibn Manjuwayh informed us: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab narrated to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, Sahl ibn Hamzah narrated to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Abu al-Zahiriyyah, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The jinn are of three kinds: one kind has wings and flies in the air; a second kind are snakes and dogs; and a third kind settle and move about." [[Mustadrak al-Hakim: 2/456.]]

﴿So when they came into its presence, they said﴾, that is, some of them said to others: "Be silent!" So they were silent and listened to the Qur'an, until some of them nearly fell upon others from the intensity of their eagerness, similar to what is in Surat al-Jinn.

﴿So when it was finished﴾, that is, when he had finished reciting the Qur'an and the jinn had finished listening. Luhaq ibn Hamid read "qada" with a fatha on the qaf and the dad, meaning the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿they turned back to their people as warners﴾, warning and calling them by the command of the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿They said: "O our people, we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what came before it, guiding to the truth and to a straight path. O our people, respond to the summoner of God﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ),

﴿and believe in him; He will forgive you some of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: So there answered them from above them about seventy men from the jinn, and they returned to the Messenger of God and met him at al-Batha'. He recited the Qur'an to them, and commanded and forbade them. The scholars differed concerning the ruling on believing jinn. Some said: The believing jinn have no reward except being saved from the Fire, and they interpreted His saying: ﴿He will forgive you some of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.﴾ This was the view of Abu Hanifah.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Manjuwayh informed us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Najawayh narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Thawr and Ibrahim ibn Abi Sufyan narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Farbani narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, who said: The reward of the jinn is that they are protected from the Fire, then it is said to them: "Be dust, like the beasts."

Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Thaqafi al-Dinawari informed us: Abu ʿAli ibn Habash al-Muqri narrated to us, Muhammad ibn ʿImran narrated to us, Ibn al-Muqri and Abu ʿUbayd Allah narrated to us, both saying: al-ʿAbdi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: The jinn enter Paradise and eat and drink.

﴿And whoever does not respond to the summoner of God, he cannot escape on earth, and he has no protectors besides Him. Those are in manifest error.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 46, verses 33–35:

﴿Have they not considered that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and did not tire in creating them, is able to give life to the dead?﴾ That is, He did not weaken in originating them and was not incapable of bringing them into being.

﴿Is He not able (bi-qadir)?﴾ The common reading is with the *ba'* (bi-) and the *alif* after the qaf, reading the word as a noun (ism). The scholars differed on the function of the *ba'* here.

Abu 'Ubayda and al-Akhfash said that the *ba'* is *silah* (a redundant, supplementary particle), as in the verse ﴿a tree that grows with oil﴾ [23:20], and as the poet al-Harith ibn Hilliza said:

*"It was said, 'What is it today that has whitened the eyes of the people, in which there is resentment and refusal?'"*

He meant: "whitened the eyes of the people."

Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said that the *ba'* here is the one that brings in the interrogative and negative at the beginning of the sentence, as in the verse ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them?﴾ [36:81]. The Arabs use it in negation when the negative governs what precedes it, as the poet said:

*"Their caravan has not returned disappointed; Hakim ibn al-Musayyab is its destination."*

Al-A'raj, 'Asim al-Jahdari, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Ya'qub ibn Ishaq read *yaqdir* with the *ya'* and without the *alif*, treating it as a verb. Abu 'Ubayd preferred the reading of the common people, because in the reading of 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) it is: ﴿who created the heavens and the earth is able﴾ without the *ba'*.

﴿…to give life to the dead? Yes! Indeed, He is over all things competent.﴾

﴿And on the Day the disbelievers are exposed to the Fire, it will be said to them: "Is this not the truth?" They will say: "Yes, by our Lord." He will say: "Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve."﴾

﴿So be patient, as the steadfast of the messengers were patient﴾ [46:35].

Ibn 'Abbas said: "those of resolve (ulu al-'azm)" are "those of determination." Al-Dahhak said: "those of diligence and patience." Al-Qurazi said: "those of judgment and correctness."

They differed about who they are. Ibn Zayd said: all the messengers were of resolve, and Allah did not send any messenger who was not of resolve. This is the view chosen by 'Ali ibn Mahdi al-Tabari, who said: "The particle *min* (of/from) is here for specification of kind (tajnis), not partition (tab'id), as one says: 'I bought cloaks of silk (khazz) and garments of cloth (bazz).'" Our shaykh Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib related this from him.

Others said: all the prophets (peace be upon them) were of resolve except Yunus (Jonah). Do you not see that our Prophet (ﷺ) forbade that one be like him, because of the haste and impatience that appeared in him when he left his people in anger? So Allah tested him with three things: the Amalekites (al-'Amaliqa) were given power over him until they raided his family and wealth; a wolf was given power over his children and it devoured them; and a fish was given power over him until it swallowed him.

I heard Abu Mansur al-Jamshadhi relate it, from Abu Bakr al-Razi, from Abu al-Qasim al-Hakim.

It was also said: they are the noble messengers mentioned in Surah al-An'am, and they are eighteen. This is the view chosen by al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl, who said: because of His saying after it: ﴿Those are the ones Allah guided, so follow their guidance﴾ [6:90].

Al-Kalbi said: they are those who were commanded to fight, so they openly declared (their message), struggled against the disbelievers by disavowing them, and fought them.

Ibn Munjawayh al-Dinawari related to us, from Abu 'Ali Habash al-Muqri, who said: Some people of knowledge said: "Ulu al-'azm" were twelve prophets who were sent to the Children of Israel in al-Sham (Greater Syria), and they disobeyed them. Allah the Exalted revealed to the prophets (peace be upon them): "I am sending My punishment upon the disobedient Children of Israel." This grieved them, so Allah revealed to them: "Choose for yourselves: if you wish, I will send the punishment upon you and save the Children of Israel; and if you wish, I will save you and send it upon the Children of Israel." They consulted among themselves, and their opinion agreed that the punishment should descend upon them and that the Children of Israel should be saved. So Allah saved the Children of Israel and sent the punishment upon those (prophets). He gave the kings of the earth power over them: some were sawn with saws, some had the skin of their heads and faces flayed, some were raised on wooden crosses, and some were burned with fire.

It was also said: they are six: Nuh (Noah), Hud, Salih, Lut (Lot), Shu'ayb, and Musa (Moses).

They are mentioned in sequence in Surah al-A'raf [the text reads "al-A'raab," as in the manuscript] and al-Shu'ara'. It was also said: they are the possessors of the sacred laws (ashab al-shara'i'), and they are five: Nuh, Ibrahim (Abraham), Musa, 'Isa (Jesus), and Muhammad (ﷺ).

Muqatil said: "Ulu al-'azm" are six: Nuh endured the harm of his people, for they used to beat him until he fainted; Ibrahim endured the fire; Ishaq endured being sacrificed; Ya'qub endured the loss of his son and the loss of his sight; Yusuf endured in the well and in prison; and Ayyub endured his affliction.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: they are four: Ibrahim, Musa, Dawud (David), and 'Isa. As for Ibrahim, his resolve was that when he was told: ﴿Submit,﴾ he said: ﴿I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [2:131]. Then he was tested in his wealth, his children, his homeland, and himself, and he was found truthful and faithful in all that he was tested with. As for Musa, his resolve was in his saying when his people said to him: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken﴾ [26:61], and he said: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [26:62]. As for Dawud, his resolve was that he committed a sin, was warned about it, and remained for forty years in grief over his sin until a tree grew from his tears, and he sat under its shade. As for 'Isa, his resolve was that he never laid a brick upon a brick in this world, and he said: "This is a passage, so cross it and do not build upon it." So Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿So be patient, as the steadfast of the messengers were patient﴾ — meaning: be truthful in what you have been tested with, like the truthfulness of Ibrahim; be confident in the victory of your Master, like the confidence of Musa; be concerned about the past slips of your conduct, like the concern of Dawud; and be ascetic in this world, like the asceticism of 'Isa (peace be upon him).

Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Jamshadhi related to us, in the same wording, that Abu 'Amr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qadi informed us, that Abu 'Abd al-Rahman informed us, that Ibn Abi al-Rabi' informed us, that 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, that Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, concerning His saying: ﴿So be patient, as the steadfast of the messengers were patient﴾ — he said: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and 'Isa (peace be upon them).

Abu Mansur al-Jamshadhi informed us, that Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Daqqaq informed us, that al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jabir informed us, that 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim related to us, that Wakee' related to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya, concerning His saying: ﴿So be patient, as the steadfast of the messengers were patient﴾ — he said: They were three: Nuh, Ibrahim, and Hud, and Muhammad was the fourth of them; he was commanded to be patient as they were patient.

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Munjawayh informed me, that Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Barza related to us, that al-Harith ibn Abi Usama related to us, that Dawud ibn al-Mukhbir related to us, that Sulayman ibn al-Hakam related to us, from al-Ahwas ibn Hakim ibn Ka'b al-Habr, who said: "In the Garden of Eden there is a city of white pearl, whose sight the eyes cannot grasp. No prophet sent (as messenger) nor any angel brought near has seen it. Allah the Glorious and Exalted prepared it for the ulu al-'azm among the messengers, the martyrs, and the strivers, because they surpassed people in intellect, forbearance, repentance, and discernment."

﴿So do not seek to hasten (the punishment) for them.﴾ That is: do not hasten the punishment for them, for it will surely descend upon them without doubt. ﴿On the Day they see what they were promised (of punishment in the Hereafter), it will be as if they had not remained (in the world) except an hour of a day﴾ — meaning, in comparison to the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: because the terror of what they witnessed will make them forget the length of their stay in the world. Then He said: ﴿A proclamation (balagh)﴾ — that is, this Qur'an and what it contains of clarification is a message that Muhammad (ﷺ) conveyed to you from Allah the Exalted. Its proof and parallel is in Surah Ibrahim.

﴿…(peace be upon him)﴾ — ﴿So will anyone be destroyed by the punishment when it descends except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾ — those who go beyond the command of Allah the Exalted.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hadithi related to us, that Sa'd ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sayrafi related to us, that Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn Abi Shayba related to us, that Minjab ibn al-Harith related to us, that 'Ali ibn Mahir related to us, that Ibn Abi Layla related to us, from al-Hakam, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "If a woman has difficulty in childbirth, let her write these two verses and these words on a sheet, then wash it off, and let her drink from it: *In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no deity except Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Mighty Throne*﴾ [23:86]."

﴿As if they had not remained, on the Day they see what they were promised, except an hour of a day. A proclamation. So will anyone be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾

I heard Abu Mansur al-Jamshadhi relate it, from Abu Bakr al-Razi, from Abu al-Qasim al-Hakim.

It was also said: they are the noble messengers mentioned in Surah al-An'am, and they are eighteen. This is the view chosen by al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl, who said: because of His saying after it: ﴿Those are the ones Allah guided, so follow their guidance﴾ [6:90].

Al-Kalbi said: they are those who were commanded to fight, so they openly declared (their message), struggled against the disbelievers by disavowing them, and fought them.

Ibn Munjawayh al-Dinawari related to us, from Abu 'Ali Habash al-Muqri, who said: Some people of knowledge said: "Ulu al-'azm" were twelve prophets who were sent to the Children of Israel in al-Sham (Greater Syria), and they disobeyed them. Allah the Exalted revealed to the prophets (peace be upon them): "I am sending My punishment upon the disobedient Children of Israel." This grieved them, so Allah revealed to them: "Choose for yourselves: if you wish, I will send the punishment upon you and save the Children of Israel; and if you wish, I will save you and send it upon the Children of Israel." They consulted among themselves, and their opinion agreed that the punishment should descend upon them and that the Children of Israel should be saved. So Allah saved the Children of Israel and sent the punishment upon those (prophets). He gave the kings of the earth power over them: some were sawn with saws, some had the skin of their heads and faces flayed, some were raised on wooden crosses, and some were burned with fire.

It was also said: they are six: Nuh (Noah), Hud, Salih, Lut (Lot), Shu'ayb, and Musa (Moses).

They are mentioned in sequence in Surah al-A'raf [the text reads "al-A'raab," as in the manuscript] and al-Shu'ara'. It was also said: they are the possessors of the sacred laws (ashab al-shara'i'), and they are five: Nuh, Ibrahim (Abraham), Musa, 'Isa (Jesus), and Muhammad (ﷺ).

Muqatil said: "Ulu al-'azm" are six: Nuh endured the harm of his people, for they used to beat him until he fainted; Ibrahim endured the fire; Ishaq endured being sacrificed; Ya'qub endured the loss of his son and the loss of his sight; Yusuf endured in the well and in prison; and Ayyub endured his affliction.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: they are four: Ibrahim, Musa, Dawud (David), and 'Isa. As for Ibrahim, his resolve was that when he was told: ﴿Submit,﴾ he said: ﴿I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [2:131]. Then he was tested in his wealth, his children, his homeland, and himself, and he was found truthful and faithful in all that he was tested with. As for Musa, his resolve was in his saying when his people said to him: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken﴾ [26:61], and he said: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [26:62]. As for Dawud, his resolve was that he committed a sin, was warned about it, and remained for forty years in grief over his sin until a tree grew from his tears, and he sat under its shade. As for 'Isa, his resolve was that he never laid a brick upon a brick in this world, and he said: "This is a passage, so cross it and do not build upon it." So Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿So be patient, as the steadfast of the messengers were patient﴾ — meaning: be truthful in what you have been tested with, like the truthfulness of Ibrahim; be confident in the victory of your Master, like the confidence of Musa; be concerned about the past slips of your conduct, like the concern of Dawud; and be ascetic in this world, like the asceticism of 'Isa (peace be upon him).

Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Jamshadhi related to us, in the same wording, that Abu 'Amr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qadi informed us, that Abu 'Abd al-Rahman informed us, that Ibn Abi al-Rabi' informed us, that 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, that Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, concerning His saying: ﴿So be patient, as the steadfast of the messengers were patient﴾ — he said: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and 'Isa (peace be upon them).

Abu Mansur al-Jamshadhi informed us, that Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Daqqaq informed us, that al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jabir informed us, that 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim related to us, that Wakee' related to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya, concerning His saying: ﴿So be patient, as the steadfast of the messengers were patient﴾ — he said: They were three: Nuh, Ibrahim, and Hud, and Muhammad was the fourth of them; he was commanded to be patient as they were patient.

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Munjawayh informed me, that Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Barza related to us, that al-Harith ibn Abi Usama related to us, that Dawud ibn al-Mukhbir related to us, that Sulayman ibn al-Hakam related to us, from al-Ahwas ibn Hakim ibn Ka'b al-Habr, who said: "In the Garden of Eden there is a city of white pearl, whose sight the eyes cannot grasp. No prophet sent (as messenger) nor any angel brought near has seen it. Allah the Glorious and Exalted prepared it for the ulu al-'azm among the messengers, the martyrs, and the strivers, because they surpassed people in intellect, forbearance, repentance, and discernment."

﴿So do not seek to hasten (the punishment) for them.﴾ That is: do not hasten the punishment for them, for it will surely descend upon them without doubt. ﴿On the Day they see what they were promised (of punishment in the Hereafter), it will be as if they had not remained (in the world) except an hour of a day﴾ — meaning, in comparison to the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: because the terror of what they witnessed will make them forget the length of their stay in the world. Then He said: ﴿A proclamation (balagh)﴾ — that is, this Qur'an and what it contains of clarification is a message that Muhammad (ﷺ) conveyed to you from Allah the Exalted. Its proof and parallel is in Surah Ibrahim.

﴿…(peace be upon him)﴾ — ﴿So will anyone be destroyed by the punishment when it descends except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾ — those who go beyond the command of Allah the Exalted.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hadithi related to us, that Sa'd ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sayrafi related to us, that Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn Abi Shayba related to us, that Minjab ibn al-Harith related to us, that 'Ali ibn Mahir related to us, that Ibn Abi Layla related to us, from al-Hakam, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "If a woman has difficulty in childbirth, let her write these two verses and these words on a sheet, then wash it off, and let her drink from it: *In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no deity except Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Mighty Throne*﴾ [23:86]."

﴿As if they had not remained, on the Day they see what they were promised, except an hour of a day. A proclamation. So will anyone be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾
